title: Trump administration accelerates criminal probe into Alaska Senate race
full_text:
By Andrew Goudsward and Nathan Frandino
WASHINGTON/ANCHORAGE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump’s administration stepped up criminal and civil investigations into allegations that Democrats conspired to recruit a spoiler candidate in a critical Senate race in Alaska, officials said on Friday, injecting fresh uncertainty into Tuesday’s midterm elections.
The top federal prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a press conference that a Wednesday New York Times article about the effort had driven a "surge" of FBI resources, adding that he had assigned several prosecutors to the case and that investigative steps were taking place "intensely and swiftly."
"Every Alaskan deserves a fair election, and they’re going to get one," he said. "Anyone who tries to illegally deceive voters and interfere with the election, they’ll answer for it."
The Alaska contest is widely seen as one of the US Senate races that could sway control of the chamber, now narrowly held by Trump’s Republicans.
TRUMP ORDERED SUIT, CLAIMS ’FRAUD AT HIGHEST LEVEL’
The Justice Department’s legal actions in Alaska and California, where the Trump administration is trying to prevent some ballots from being counted, represent an extraordinary federal intervention in state-run elections, which are administered locally under the US Constitution.
When the DOJ filed the civil suit against Alaska a week ago, Trump told reporters, "I’m the one that said do it."
Heyman declined to offer specifics when asked what possible crimes were being examined, saying he would let the Alaska investigation proceed, although Trump has called for a prosecution of Senate candidate Mary Peltola, a Democrat.
"This is voter fraud at the highest level," Trump told a Florida rally on Friday.
The Department of Justice asked a federal judge on Friday to ensure the preservation of ballots that "may be impacted by voter confusion." The court filing requested the judge’s help obtaining documents from the Democratic campaign and others to determine "whether Daniel J. Sullivan’s candidacy is frivolous or fraudulent."
The DOJ also has sued Alaska to preemptively block the state from certifying the results of the Senate race if the Republican incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, loses due to the presence of a third candidate, named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
It is not clear what, if any, laws may have been broken. Both parties have engaged in "ballot stacking" by propping up lesser-known candidates to siphon votes from their opponents.
If Democrats take one or both chambers of Congress, they intend to launch investigations of the Trump administration and increase pressure on the president to end the war against Iran.
The New York Times reported this week that staffers from the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Party’s Senate campaign arm helped recruit Daniel J. Sullivan Jr, a retired teacher living in a remote fishing village, to appear on the ballot. Reuters has not independently confirmed the Times’ reporting.
Peltola has denied knowing about any effort to recruit the second Sullivan, and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has also denied involvement. The retired teacher has denied coordinating with Peltola’s campaign.
SURGE OF VOTING NATIONWIDE DESPITE UNCERTAINTY
Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are bracing for further disruptions from the Trump administration, which has sued about 30 states seeking unredacted voter rolls.
“The new tactic is just to create enough confusion and enough uncertainty and enough doubt through the filing of all these lawsuits to lay the groundwork to ultimately, I think, challenge the results once the dust settles after Tuesday," said Jonathan Diaz of the nonpartisan Campaign Legal Center.
Trump has long sought to sow distrust of election results, falsely claiming for years that his 2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Biden was the result of widespread fraud. Voter fraud in the US is extremely rare, studies and investigations have found.
Despite any uncertainty, a record 49 million people have cast early ballots, more than any other midterm election in US history, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab, with even the American-born Pope Leo casting a ballot by mail.
The DOJ has also pushed forward a legal case in California, issuing subpoenas to election officials as part of a criminal probe into alleged voting by noncitizens, according to copies of documents seen by Reuters.
A US appeals court on Friday rejected the department’s request to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens, the second time the court has done so this week.
A lower court judge had denied the administration’s request, finding it would potentially disenfranchise thousands of legal voters.
Trump said on Friday he would attend weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas, a day after canceling them, telling reporters at the White House that Republicans in those states had called him and asked him to reconsider.

title: Iranian envoys meet Qatari mediators as threat looms of US strikes after midterms
full_text:
By Andrew Mills, Yasmine Ghania and Enas Alashray
DUBAI/CAIRO, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert a new outbreak of fighting after the US midterm elections this week.
Saturday’s talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who was briefed on the negotiations and spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington.
Countries in the region have been anticipating that US President Donald Trump, who has held off on strikes on Iran during the weeks leading up to Tuesday’s midterm elections, could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.
Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.
"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response," Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since replacing his father slain at the war’s outset, said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account.
He said that senior commanders had reported high readiness along the Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran’s northwestern and southeastern borders.
DIPLOMACY CONTINUES DESPITE GAPS
Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can "finish the job".
But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to a hardline senior Iranian security official, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it was possible to restart talks.
Trump played the letter down, saying he approved it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: "I said if you want to do that, that’s ok. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well."
In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would take daily steps to build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.
Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade of Iranian ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which the contested strait would be reopened.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance’s letter. He said the Iranian plan was the only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.

title: Binance says it has replaced 90% of $6.3 billion stolen in record crypto hack
full_text:
The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange reiterated on Saturday that it would absorb the entire financial impact of the theft, pledging that users would not suffer losses.
News of the breach triggered broad selling across cryptocurrency markets on Friday, with Bitcoin hitting a six-week low of $76,469.82 and trading around 3% lower. Ether also fell more than 3%, while other major cryptocurrencies came under pressure.
In a social media update, Binance said it had been replenishing affected assets, including Bitcoin, Zcash and stablecoins USDT and USDC. The replacement funds have come from a combination of the company’s treasury, emergency reserves and insurance funds.
The latest update marks progress from the exchange’s previous disclosure that it had covered approximately 80% of the stolen assets. Binance said the remaining tokens were less liquid, making them more difficult to source and replace.
The exchange also said it was working to restore withdrawals by Sunday. The service had been suspended as part of its response to the incident, while Binance worked to contain the impact and replenish the affected assets.
“Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not users,” the company said in its post.
The incident has sent shockwaves through the cryptocurrency industry. At $6.3 billion, the theft is being described by experts as the largest hack in cryptocurrency history and one of the biggest cyber incidents more broadly.
The scale of the breach comes as digital asset firms seek wider mainstream adoption, putting renewed attention on the security of crypto platforms and the protection of customer funds.
Binance’s commitment to make users whole and its plan to resume withdrawals are key steps in its effort to restore confidence following the attack.

title: Meta builds humanoid robot with China’s Fourier as home robot push expands: report
full_text:
Investing.com -- Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) has developed a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics startup Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported on Saturday, as the Facebook parent steps up efforts to bring AI into everyday household tasks.
The prototype, internally named Max, weighs about 106 pounds and was built by the two companies in roughly three months, according to people familiar with the project cited by The Information.
Standing around 1.5 metres tall, the robot uses Nvidia’s Jetson Thor chip and features a display capable of mimicking facial expressions, built-in speakers and five-fingered hands designed to handle small objects, according to the report.
Meta's robotics team travelled to China to work with Fourier, with the company's vice president of product for robotics, Li-Chen Miller, spending almost two months at the startup's Shanghai factory, the report said. Max was demonstrated to some Meta employees at an internal robotics summit in late August.
The companies began developing a second prototype, Max 2, in September. The updated version is expected to feature a redesigned torso, improved hands for handling objects, a projector and additional sensors to help it navigate stairs, according to the report.
Meta sees humanoid robots as a potential physical extension of its Muse AI agent, with the long-term ambition of developing machines capable of assisting with household tasks. The company has also strengthened its robotics capabilities through its May acquisition of Assured Robot Intelligence, a startup developing AI models that help robots understand and adapt to human behaviour.
However, Meta told The Information that its work with Fourier was focused on internal research and experimentation and that it had no plans to sell the units.

title: Thousands return to Lisbon square, press government to scrap rental bill
full_text:
By Sergio Goncalves and Rodrigo Antunes
LISBON, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Thousands of housing protesters returned to one of Lisbon’s main squares on Saturday, stepping up pressure on Portugal’s minority centre-right government to scrap a rental bill they say would worsen the country’s affordability crisis.
Portugal is grappling with one of Europe’s worst housing crises, with young people among those hardest hit. House prices have more than doubled since 2017 and rents for new leases have nearly doubled.
Organisers said several thousand people packed Rossio Square in central Lisbon. Police gave no crowd estimate.
Housing protests have intensified in recent weeks. Police have been criticized for baton-charging demonstrators and arresting dozens while clearing a similar tent camp in the same square a week ago.
Rita Silva, a spokesperson for housing movement Casa para Viver, told public broadcaster RTP that "people are showing enormous perseverance, strength and determination" after weeks of protests over the housing crisis, rising living costs and "the enormous difficulty of making a living today".
"We are not seeing any willingness from the government to listen ...the demonstrations will continue," she said.
The unrest mirrors protests across Spain, France, Germany and elsewhere in Europe over soaring housing costs.
Interior Minister Luis Neves said the government respected the legitimacy of the protests but expected them to be held "with order, civility" and "in compliance with the law."
SCRAP THE BILL
The protesters are demanding the government scrap a bill making evictions easier and ending rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading with the abstention of the far-right Chega party.
Prime Minister Luis Montenegro on Thursday ruled out scrapping the bill but said he was open to amending it ahead of a final vote in coming weeks, saying parties "have to move closer" while making clear "the main line of action is the government’s programme".
Socialist Party leader Jose Luis Carneiro urged the government on Saturday to engage in talks with opposition parties and protesters rather than "arrogantly imposing its views, sometimes even with authoritarian overtones".

title: Why the sell-off in French bonds is a warning for global governments
full_text:
Investing.com -- The sell-off in French government bonds is a warning that investors are becoming less tolerant of heavy borrowing and persistent budget deficits, with the episode potentially pushing governments elsewhere to accelerate spending cuts and fiscal consolidation, Capital Economics said.
In a research note, the consultancy's Chief Global Economist Jennifer McKeown said France's difficulties were unlikely to trigger a broader fiscal crisis, given that few other advanced economies combine similarly weak public finances with such limited political room to rein in spending.
However, the fallout could weigh on global economic growth in the coming years.
France's gross government debt is estimated at 118% of GDP in 2026, below levels in Japan, Italy and the U.S. and broadly comparable with the UK. Its fiscal position stands out because of the scale of its borrowing despite the already elevated debt burden.
The International Monetary Fund expects France to run a primary budget deficit, which excludes interest payments, of 2.8% of GDP this year, compared with a 1.4% deficit in the UK and a 1% surplus in Italy.
To stabilise its debt ratio, France would need to bring its primary budget balance close to zero, requiring a substantial fiscal adjustment. Capital Economics said no other major advanced economy faced a comparable gap between its current primary balance and the level needed to stabilise debt.
Political constraints are adding to the pressure. President Emmanuel Macron's government lacks a majority in the National Assembly and has struggled to pass a budget, while proposed spending reductions have faced resistance and protests. Investors are also concerned about the prospect of greater fiscal populism ahead of next year's presidential election, with Marine Le Pen currently the frontrunner, the consultancy said.
Capital Economics expects France's headline budget deficit to remain close to its current 5.4%, rather than fall significantly.
A French fiscal crisis could have international consequences because foreign investors hold roughly 60% of the country's marketable sovereign debt, equivalent to around €1.6 trillion. About half of those holdings are outside the euro zone.
A sharp decline in bond prices could generate losses for banks, insurers and investment funds, potentially eroding capital and prompting asset sales. However, the consultancy considers the risk of a systemic shock to be low because holdings are widely distributed.

title: Countries reach COP17 deal to speed up biodiversity action, but money still short
full_text:
By Simon Jessop and Virginia Furness
LONDON, Oct 31 (Reuters) - Governments at a UN conference that ended on Saturday have agreed to step up efforts to protect global biodiversity after talks ran through the night, although the finance to deliver it remains elusive.
The two-week COP17 conference in Armenia’s capital came against a fractious political backdrop, and as the world prepares for fresh climate talks in Turkey starting November 9.
The talks in Yerevan oversaw the first global review of the Global Biodiversity Framework agreed in Montreal four years ago. While progress had been made, delegates agreed it was not enough, with the world off track on almost all of its targets.
After intense talks, governments adopted a decision dubbed the Yerevan Pathway, agreeing faster action on areas such as reducing harmful subsidies, increasing finance for developing countries, and aligning national spending with biodiversity goals.
They acknowledged that action so far had been insufficient, and set out priorities to accelerate efforts through to 2030.
"At a time when multilateralism is under pressure, COP17 has shown that international cooperation can still deliver," said Anita de Horde, executive director of the Finance for Biodiversity Foundation.
"The real success of COP17 will be measured by what governments implement before COP18," she said, which delegates agreed would be held in the Ecuadorean capital, Quito, in 2028.
The framework agreed in Montreal set goals including conserving 30% of land, inland waters, marine and coastal areas by 2030, restoring 30% of degraded ecosystems, reforming harmful subsidies, and mobilising $200 billion a year to help pay to preserve biodiversity.
Nearly 90% of parties to the biodiversity convention had set national targets, although fewer than half of those assessed were on track, the UN said.
REVIEW SENT ’STRONG SIGNAL’
Daudi Sumba, chief conservation officer at WWF International, said the review of progress had sent a "strong signal", but it needed to be backed up with finance.
Organisers said more than $1.8 billion in finance from governments, philanthropies and investors had been announced during the conference.
On the issue of biodiversity-harming subsidies, governments agreed to accelerate efforts towards the existing target of reducing harmful incentives by at least $500 billion a year by 2030.
Delegates also agreed to review existing funding arrangements, set criteria for a future permanent financing mechanism and voluntarily broaden the contributor base, although some said progress overall remained too slow.
"We cannot just plod on to 2030 without a course correction," said Catherine Weller, global policy director at non-profit Fauna & Flora.

title: OPEC+ set to hold December oil output steady, Reuters reports
full_text:
Investing.com -- OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to maintain their December oil production targets, as the alliance is expected to hold off on further supply policy changes until next year, Reuters reported on Saturday, citing three people familiar with the matter.
The agreement is expected to be discussed at an online meeting on Sunday involving seven core members: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, according to the Reuters report.
The decision comes as Gulf producers work to boost exports that have been disrupted for months by the war involving Iran. Most members are still producing below their assigned targets despite efforts to restore shipments.
OPEC+ completed the phased unwinding of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day production cut in September, which was first agreed in 2023. However, the group continues to maintain another layer of reductions totalling around 2 million bpd, covering most members through the end of 2026, Reuters reported.
The alliance is also preparing to shift its focus towards negotiations over production quotas for 2027. OPEC+ is expected to finalise a review of members’ production capacity during the fourth quarter before establishing new baselines that will determine future output quotas and plans to unwind the remaining cuts, according to Reuters.
Reuters reported in July that OPEC+ was likely to leave its production targets unchanged throughout the fourth quarter as it turned its attention to the 2027 quota discussions.
The decision to maintain December targets would therefore preserve the group’s current production policy while members prepare for next year’s negotiations.

title: Top takeaways from Bernstein’s annual Global Sportswear survey
full_text:
Investing.com -- Sportswear spending is expected to rise in 2027, particularly in China and the U.S.. Still, demand for premium products is increasingly concentrated among younger and wealthier consumers, Bernstein’s annual global survey showed.
Bernstein surveyed 3,200 sportswear buyers across the U.S., China, the UK and Germany, examining spending plans, exercise habits and brand preferences in the $420 billion industry.
China led expectations for higher spending next year, with 56% of respondents planning to spend more, followed by 49% in the U.S., 40% in the UK and 28% in Germany.
Only 10% of Chinese respondents expected to spend less, compared with 23% in the U.S., 22% in the UK and 25% in Germany.
More frequent exercise was the leading reason for planned spending increases. Consumers expecting to cut purchases most often cited already owning enough sportswear or seeking cheaper products.
Bernstein found that younger shoppers and higher-income groups continued to exercise more frequently, contrasting with slowing activity among consumers aged 45 and older.
Sneaker ownership also increased across most markets as athletic footwear gained acceptance at work, school and dressier occasions. U.S. sneaker-wearing frequency was broadly flat amid interest in more formal styles.
Willingness to pay premium prices strengthened most in the U.S., particularly among affluent consumers, but softened at the highest price points in Europe and China.
Nike retained the strongest overall brand perceptions, ranking first in the U.S. for performance, quality, fashion and value, although its standing weakened in China.
Adidas remained particularly strong in Germany, and Lululemon improved in fashion rankings and across categories in China.
Among challengers, On gained ground in Germany and China, Hoka improved in quality and performance across Western markets, and Alo posted its strongest gains in the UK. Vuori’s ratings weakened in the U.S. and Germany.
Bernstein rates Nike, Adidas, and On Outperform, and Lululemon and Deckers Market-Perform.
